authority.name: Office of the State Superintendent of Education

curriculum.name: District of Columbia Grade 3 Mathematics — Common Core State Standards

expectations.title: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division
expectations.description: Interpret products and quotients of whole numbers, use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems, and determine unknown whole numbers in equations.

expectations.title: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
expectations.description: Understand fractions 1/b and a/b, represent fractions on a number line, and explain equivalence and comparison of fractions.

expectations.title: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area
expectations.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures, understand concepts of area measurement, and relate area to multiplication and addition.

skills.name: Multiplication as Equal Groups
skills.description: Interpret products as equal groups and arrays.

canonical.name: Multiplication as Equal Groups
canonical.description: Understand multiplication as equal groups, arrays, and repeated addition.

problems.prompt: A Metro train has 4 cars with 6 seats in each car. How many seats are on the train?
problems.objective: Diagnose whether the learner interprets an equal-groups product.

problems.prompt: A bakery packs 5 boxes with 3 muffins in each box. How many muffins are packed in all?
problems.objective: Guide the learner from a context to an equal-groups product.

problems.prompt: A library shelf has 7 rows with 4 books in each row. How many books are on the shelf?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of equal-groups multiplication.

problems.prompt: A school garden has 6 rows with 5 tomato plants in each row. How many tomato plants are there?
problems.objective: Verify mastery of equal-groups multiplication in context.

skills.name: Division as Equal Sharing
skills.description: Interpret quotients through fair sharing and groups of a known size.

canonical.name: Division as Equal Sharing
canonical.description: Understand division as fair sharing and as finding an unknown group size or number of groups.

problems.prompt: Twenty cherry blossom stickers are shared equally among 4 classmates. How many stickers does each classmate get?
Thirty library bookmarks are placed into groups of 5. How many groups are made?
problems.objective: Guide the learner to interpret quotative division.

problems.prompt: Twenty-four tour tickets are packed equally into 6 envelopes. How many tickets are in each envelope?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of equal-sharing division.

problems.prompt: A coach places 36 cones in rows of 9. How many rows are made?
problems.objective: Verify mastery of equal-sharing division in context.

skills.name: Unit Fractions as Numbers
skills.description: Understand 1/b as one equal part of a whole and build fractions from it.

canonical.name: Unit Fractions as Numbers
canonical.description: Understand unit fractions 1/b and build non-unit fractions a/b from unit fractions.

problems.prompt: A rectangular garden is divided into 3 equal parts. What fraction is one part?
problems.objective: Diagnose understanding of 1/b as one equal part.

problems.prompt: One equal slice of a pizza is 1/8. How many equal slices make the whole pizza?
problems.objective: Guide the learner to connect unit fractions to the whole.

problems.prompt: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 6 equal spaces. What fraction names the first mark after 0?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of unit fractions on a number line.

problems.prompt: Diego uses 4 pieces of size 1/5 to make a banner. What fraction of the banner does he have?
problems.objective: Verify mastery of building non-unit fractions from unit fractions.

skills.name: Rectangle Area with Unit Squares
skills.description: Relate rectangular arrays, unit squares, and multiplication to area.

canonical.name: Rectangle Area with Unit Squares
canonical.description: Understand area as covering with unit squares and relate it to multiplication.

problems.prompt: A classroom rug has 3 rows of 6 unit squares. What is its area in square units?
problems.objective: Diagnose understanding of area as rows of unit squares.

problems.prompt: A poster is 5 units long and 2 units wide. What is its area?
problems.objective: Guide the learner to multiply length and width for area.

problems.prompt: A hallway covers 4 rows with 8 unit squares in each row. What area does it cover?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of rectangle area reasoning.

problems.prompt: A desktop is 7 units by 3 units. Find its area in square units.
problems.objective: Verify mastery of rectangle area with unit squares.
